turns.prompt: My basil plants keep dying on the windowsill. Can you explain what basil actually needs?
turns.response:
Basil wants **sun, warmth, and moist soil that drains well**. A windowsill can provide the sun while being too cold for it—rather an annoying arrangement. ([yardandgarden.extension.iastate.edu](https://yardandgarden.extension.iastate.edu/how-to/growing-basil-home-garden?utm_source=openai))

Here’s what matters:

- **Real sunlight, not just a bright room.** Aim for at least six hours of direct sun each day. If the window can’t supply enough, a grow light can help. ([extension.umd.edu](https://www.extension.umd.edu/resource/growing-basil-home-garden?utm_source=openai))
- **Warmth, especially near the glass.** Keep it away from cold draughts and cold windowpanes. Basil is more cold-sensitive than many other windowsill herbs. ([chicagobotanic.org](https://www.chicagobotanic.org/plantinfo/tips/growing_herbs_your_windowsill?utm_source=openai))
- **Moist roots, not permanently soaked roots.** Check the soil rather than watering on a fixed schedule: let it begin drying before watering again, without leaving the whole pot parched. Persistently wet soil deprives roots of oxygen. ([ask.extension.org](https://ask.extension.org/kb/faq.php?id=904518&utm_source=openai))
- **A pot with drainage holes.** Water must be able to escape; don’t leave the pot sitting in standing water. ([extension.illinois.edu](https://extension.illinois.edu/container-gardens/growing-herbs-containers?utm_source=openai))
- **Regular pinching back.** Pinch off the growing tips to encourage branching, rather than letting it become one long stem. For indoor plants, a half-strength liquid fertiliser every four to six weeks is enough. ([extension.illinois.edu](https://extension.illinois.edu/herbs/basil?utm_source=openai))

I can’t tell which of those is killing yours yet. What happens first—do they wilt, turn yellow, or develop dark patches?

turns.prompt: How often should I water it, and how do I tell if I'm overdoing it?
turns.response:
**Check it daily, but don’t water it automatically.** There isn’t a reliable “every three days” rule: light, warmth, pot size and drainage change how quickly the soil dries. ([extension.illinois.edu](https://extension.illinois.edu/houseplants/watering))

For your windowsill basil:
- **Feel about an inch (2–3 cm) into the soil.** If it’s still damp, wait; if it’s starting to feel dry, water. Aim for moist soil below the surface, not a completely dried-out pot. ([web.extension.illinois.edu](https://web.extension.illinois.edu/gpe/case1/c1facts3d.html?utm_source=openai))
- **Water thoroughly, then let it drain.** Empty the saucer or outer decorative pot rather than leaving the roots sitting in water. ([extension.illinois.edu](https://extension.illinois.edu/houseplants/watering))

**Signs you may be overdoing it:**
- Leaves lose colour or drop while the soil stays wet. Those symptoms aren’t proof on their own, but wet soil makes overwatering a stronger suspect. ([extension.illinois.edu](https://extension.illinois.edu/houseplants/troubleshooting))
- It wilts **despite damp soil**. That’s the sneaky one: persistently wet conditions can damage roots, so the plant droops even though water is available. Adding more can make matters worse. ([yardandgarden.extension.iastate.edu](https://yardandgarden.extension.iastate.edu/faq/why-my-houseplant-wilting))

If it’s drooping, **touch the soil before reaching for the watering can**. ([extension.illinois.edu](https://extension.illinois.edu/houseplants/watering))

turns.prompt: Is it worth trying to grow it from seed, or are supermarket pots fine to keep going?
turns.response:
**Supermarket pots are worth keeping going—you don’t need to start from seed.** The catch is that one bushy-looking pot often contains lots of tightly packed plants. Separating and repotting them gives them more room to grow. ([gardenorganic.org.uk](https://www.gardenorganic.org.uk/how-to-grow-basil?utm_source=openai))

- **For the easiest start:** buy a healthy pot, gently divide the rootball into a few smaller clumps, and repot in fresh potting mix in pots with drainage holes. You don’t have to untangle every individual seedling. ([tollbit.gardenersworld.com](https://tollbit.gardenersworld.com/how-to/grow-plants/how-to-make-five-plants-from-one-supermarket-basil?utm_source=openai))
- **For growing from scratch:** seeds are worth trying, especially if you want different varieties. Basil needs warmth for germination and a warm, bright spot afterwards; spring is a good time to begin. ([rhs.org.uk](https://www.rhs.org.uk/herbs/basil/grow-your-own?utm_source=openai))

**I’d try dividing a supermarket pot first.** But seed-grown basil still needs the same light, warmth and drainage—changing how you start won’t fix an unsuitable windowsill. Crowding is another possible culprit, not yet a diagnosis for yours. ([rhs.org.uk](https://www.rhs.org.uk/herbs/basil/grow-your-own?utm_source=openai))
